mainTopic: Which places in and around בבל have trusted or flawed lineage, with aggadah about Persia and רבי's deathbed warnings
overview: The גמרא keeps mapping where בבל, with its trusted family lineage, begins and ends. It notes that the Persians moved the border bridge. It also brings רב יוסף's proof that בירם is fine, since the pure families of פומבדיתא marry from there. רב פפא and רב יוסף then argue whether the border dispute also applies to גיטין. Next the גמרא praises חביל ימא and its towns as the finest lineage in בבל, and it rejects a rumor that כותים mixed into them. It rules that the area 'between the rivers' and חלזון ניהוונד count like the גולה, and it settles an apparent contradiction in רבי יוחנן's borders. רבי אבא בר כהנא disagrees, because the ten tribes were exiled to those places, and the גמרא separates מושכי, which is flawed, from מושכני, which is kosher. After some aggadah on דניאל's bear and the Persians, רבי names towns in בבל with lineage problems on his deathbed, and his list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Persians moved the bridge
steps.stepSummary: A side comment: the bridge used as a border marker was moved further up by the Persians in recent times.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is only nowadays that the Persians moved it (the bridge) further up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short historical note to the earlier border discussion: the bridge that marks the edge of בבל is not where it used to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The border of בבל was set by a bridge on the פרת. The גמרא warns that the bridge you see today was moved up by the Persians. So you must measure from where the bridge originally stood, not from where it stands now.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised it / moved it up

steps.confusionAlert: Do not use today's bridge to measure the border. The border stays where the bridge was originally.

phrases.english: And it is only now that the Persians moved it up.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the bridge mentioned just before this. The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא הוּא דְּדַלְיוּהּ פָּרְסָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the border discussion from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bridge border marker was moved up by the Persians, so the original location is what counts.

steps.title: אביי asks about the western side of the Euphrates
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף how far the border of בבל goes on this side of the פרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: On this side of the Euphrates, until where does it go?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a new border question. This time it is about the other bank of the river, the side of the פרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the borders were described along the rivers. אביי wants to know how far the 'safe lineage' zone of בבל reaches on this particular bank. The question sets up רב יוסף's answer.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
On this side of the Euphrates, until where?
phrases.notes: He means the western bank of the river.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף לְהָא גִּיסָא דִפְרָת עַד הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about another side of the border.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far the lineage border of בבל extends on the western side of the פרת.

steps.title: רב יוסף: פומבדיתא's families marry from בירם
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף guesses that אביי is worried about the town of בירם, and says it has no problem: the pure families of פומבדיתא marry women from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are you thinking? Is it because of Biram? The families of pure lineage in Pumbedita marry women from Biram.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף figures out why אביי is asking. אביי must be wondering about בירם, and רב יוסף removes the worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of drawing a line, רב יוסף points to a real-life practice. The careful families of פומבדיתא take wives from בירם. That shows בירם is treated as having good lineage.

phrases.english: He said to him: What are you thinking?
Is it because of Biram?
phrases.notes: בירם is a town on that side of the river.

phrases.english: The pure-lineage families of Pumbedita marry from Biram.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ מִשּׁוּם בִּירָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בירם is fine for lineage, since the pure families of פומבדיתא marry from there.
steps.whatToRemember: How people actually behave, here pure families marrying from בירם, can show that a place has good lineage.

steps.title: רב פפא: the same border dispute applies to divorce documents
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the argument about the border of בבל for lineage also applies to the laws of גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: Just as there is a dispute regarding lineage, so there is a dispute regarding divorce documents.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes the border argument and applies it to a second area of halacha, divorce documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח bringing a גט from abroad must normally say it was written and signed in front of him, but a שליח coming from בבל does not. רב פפא says the borders of 'בבל' for this rule are the same disputed borders used for lineage.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: Just as the dispute regarding lineage,
so is the dispute regarding divorce documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא כְּמַחְלוֹקֶת לְיוּחֲסִין כָּךְ מַחְלוֹקֶת לְעִנְיַן גִּיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the earlier border argument to גיטין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The border argument applies equally to lineage and to גיטין.

steps.title: רב יוסף: for divorce documents everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the argument is only about lineage. For גיטין, everyone agrees that בבל reaches until the second lake of the bridge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף says: The dispute is regarding lineage, but regarding divorce documents, everyone agrees: until the second lake of the bridge.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף disagrees with רב פפא. He limits the argument to lineage and gives one agreed border for גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, the two areas of halacha do not share the same borders. For גיטין there is no argument, and בבל extends up to the second lake by the bridge.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef says: The dispute is regarding lineage,
but regarding divorce documents, everyone agrees:
until the second lake of the bridge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר מַחְלוֹקֶת לְיוּחֲסִין אֲבָל לְגִיטִּין דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב פפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about lineage. For גיטין, בבל reaches until the second lake of the bridge.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא: the same border argument applies to lineage and גיטין. רב יוסף: the argument is only about lineage, and for גיטין everyone agrees.

steps.title: רמי בר אבא: the glory of בבל
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא says חביל ימא is the finest region of בבל for lineage, and שוניא and גוביא are the finest towns within חביל ימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said: חביל ימא is the glory of בבל. שוניא and גוביא are the glory of חביל ימא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from borders to ranking. It names the places inside בבל with the very best lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are levels within בבל. חביל ימא stands out in all of בבל, and inside it, שוניא and גוביא stand out even more.

phrases.english: Rami bar Abba said:
Ḥaveil Yamma is the glory of Babylonia.
Shunya and Guvya are the glory of Ḥaveil Yamma.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא חֲבֵיל יַמָּא תְּכֵילְתָּא דְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from borders to ranking places by quality of lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חביל ימא is the best of בבל for lineage, and שוניא and גוביא are the best of חביל ימא.

steps.title: רבינא adds ציצורא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא adds the town of ציצורא to the top-ranked towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Also ציצורא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds one more town to רמי בר אבא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ציצורא belongs with שוניא and גוביא as the finest towns of חביל ימא.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Also Tzitzora.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר אַף צִיצוֹרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רמי בר אבא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצורא is also among the finest towns of חביל ימא.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the list
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of חנן בן פנחס says the same thing and includes ציצורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught so: חנן בן פנחס says: חביל ימא is the glory of בבל; שוניא, גוביא and ציצורא are the glory of חביל ימא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up what was just said, including רבינא's addition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats רמי בר אבא's ranking and also names ציצורא. That supports רבינא's addition.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא quoted in the ברייתא

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
Ḥanan ben Pineḥas says:
Ḥaveil Yamma is the glory of Babylonia;

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּנְיָא וְגוּבְיָא וְצִיצוֹרָא – תְּכֵילְתָּא דַּחֲבֵיל יַמָּא.
phrases.english: Shunya, Guvya and Tzitzora are the glory of Ḥaveil Yamma.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's addition.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's addition of ציצורא, together with רמי בר אבא's list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of חנן בן פנחס.

steps.title: רב פפא: Samaritans have mixed in
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that nowadays כותים have mixed into these towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: And nowadays Samaritans have mixed in with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a worry that these top towns are no longer so pure, because כותים married into them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If true, this would damage the praise just given to these towns. The claim is about the present day, not the past.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
And nowadays Samaritans have mixed in with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא וְהָאִידָּנָא אִיעָרַבִי בְּהוּ כּוּתָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a concern about the towns just praised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nowadays כותים have mixed into these towns.

steps.title: The rumor is false
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's claim. A כותי only asked to marry a woman from there, and they refused him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is not so. It was a woman that one asked for from them, and they did not give her to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא and explains how the rumor started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No mixing actually happened. A כותי asked for a wife from these towns and was refused, and people mistook the request for a marriage. The refusal actually shows how careful these towns were.

keyTerms.meaning: they did not give to him

phrases.english: And that is not so;
rather, he asked for a woman from them,
phrases.notes: 'He' is a כותי who wanted to marry into these towns.

phrases.english: and they did not give her to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's claim.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that כותים mixed into חביל ימא's towns.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It was only a request to marry, and it was refused, so no mixing happened.
steps.whatToRemember: The top towns of חביל ימא kept their pure lineage. The rumor about כותים came from a marriage request that was turned down.

steps.title: What is חביל ימא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the place called חביל ימא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is חביל ימא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the location of חביל ימא. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having praised חביל ימא, the גמרא now needs to tell us which area it means.

phrases.english: What is Ḥaveil Yamma?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חֲבֵיל יַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the location of the region praised earlier.

steps.title: רב פפא: the פרת by בורסי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says חביל ימא is the area of the פרת near בורסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is the פרת of בורסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that חביל ימא is the stretch of the פרת near the town of בורסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name points to a known area along the river. Now the earlier ranking can be tied to a real place.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: זוֹ פְּרָת דְּבוֹרְסִי.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is the Euphrates of Bursi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא זוֹ פְּרָת דְּבוֹרְסִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חביל ימא is the area of the פרת near בורסי.

steps.title: The man from שוט מישוט
steps.stepSummary: A man says he is from שוט מישוט, and רבי יצחק נפחא stands up and says that place lies between the rivers.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to them: I am from שוט מישוט. רבי יצחק נפחא stood on his feet and said: שוט מישוט is located between the rivers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. It sets up the coming question about why being 'between the rivers' matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק נפחא stood up to make a point about this man's hometown. He placed it between the rivers, but did not say why that matters. The גמרא asks next.

phrases.english: A certain man said to them:
I am from Shot Mishot.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa stood on his feet and said:
Shot Mishot is located between the rivers.
phrases.notes: The rivers are the דגלת and the פרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ אֲנָא מִן שׁוֹט מֵישׁוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שוט מישוט is between the rivers.

steps.title: So what if it is between the rivers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it makes that שוט מישוט is between the rivers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is located between the rivers, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יצחק נפחא's comment matters for halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing where a place is helps only if there is a rule attached to it. The גמרא wants that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: what of it? what difference does it make?

phrases.english: And if it is located between the rivers,
what of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בֵּין הַנְּהָרוֹת עוֹמֶדֶת מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the story's statement matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What halacha depends on a place being between the rivers.

steps.title: Between the rivers is like the גולה for lineage
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא teaches that the area between the rivers counts like the גולה for lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said that רבי חמא בר עוקבא said that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Between the rivers is like the גולה with regard to lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Being between the rivers means having trusted lineage, just like the גולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גולה here means the main Jewish area of בבל, centered on פומבדיתא, whose lineage is trusted. So רבי יצחק נפחא was confirming that the man had good lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: like the גולה, the trusted area of בבל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא,
phrases.english: Abaye said that Rabbi Ḥama bar Ukva said
that Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הַנְּהָרוֹת הֲרֵי הִיא כַּגּוֹלָה לְיוּחֲסִין.
phrases.english: Between the rivers is like the Golah with regard to lineage.
phrases.notes: The גולה here means the area around פומבדיתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The area between the rivers has trusted lineage, like the גולה.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Between the rivers' is a good-lineage area, counted like the גולה.

steps.title: Where exactly is 'between the rivers'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where this area begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is it located?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact borders of the 'between the rivers' area. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rivers are very long, so the rule needs a starting point. The question asks which stretch counts.

phrases.english: And where is it located?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא קָיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the area just discussed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The boundaries of the 'between the rivers' area.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: from איהי דקירא and upward
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the area starts at איהי דקירא and goes upward (north).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: From איהי דקירא and upward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a starting point: the area from איהי דקירא and further up the rivers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Upward' means north, upstream. This answer will be challenged next, because רבי יוחנן seems to say something different elsewhere.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
From Ihi Dekira and upward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵאִיהִי דְקִירָא וּלְעֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן said: until the crossing at גיזמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this. רבי יוחנן said elsewhere that the border is only until the crossing at גיזמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: Until the crossing at גיזמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an apparent contradiction between two statements of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, רבי יוחנן set the edge of the good-lineage area at the crossing of גיזמא. Now 'from איהי דקירא and upward' seems to reach further. Both cannot be the border.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
Until the crossing at Gizma!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן עַד מַעְבַּרְתָּא דְגִיזְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement 'from איהי דקירא and upward'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to contradict his other statement that the border is only until the crossing at גיזמא.

steps.title: אביי: a strip extends out
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a narrow strip of good-lineage land sticks out past the main border.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A strip extends out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. Both statements are true because a strip of land reaches out beyond the main border.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main border is the crossing at גיזמא. A narrow strip of land stretches out from there, and that strip also counts. So the two statements describe different parts of the same map.

phrases.english: Abaye said: A strip extends out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי רְצוּעָה נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both statements are true. One gives the main border, and the other covers a strip that sticks out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements of רבי יוחנן contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A strip of good-lineage land extends past the main border, so both are true.
steps.whatToRemember: Border lines are not always straight. A strip of land can stick out and still count as good-lineage territory.

steps.title: רב's teaching that חלזון ניהוונד has kosher lineage
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא בר אבין, quoting רב חננאל in the name of רב, says that חלזון ניהוונד counts like the גולה for lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא בר אבין said that רב חננאל said that רב said: חלזון ניהוונד is like the גולה regarding lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more place to the list of areas with kosher lineage: חלזון ניהוונד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya mapped the borders of Babylonia itself. Now a new region is declared just as good as the גולה, so Jews from there may marry into families of proven lineage without checking.

keyTerms.meaning: Lineage, meaning family purity for marriage
Like the Exile, meaning like Babylonia, which has the best lineage

phrases.english: Rav Ika bar Avin said
that Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
Chillazon Nihavnad
is like the Exile regarding lineage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new region to the lineage map after the border discussion of steps 16-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חלזון ניהוונד has the same kosher lineage status as the גולה.

steps.title: אביי says not to trust the teaching because of a personal interest
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells people to ignore רב איקא בר אבין, because a יבמה from that place fell to him for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: Do not listen to him; it is a יבמה who fell to him from there.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges whether the teacher can be trusted. He suggests רב איקא has a personal reason to call that place kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is not attacking the logic of the ruling. He is questioning the reporter: if the woman he has to marry through יבום comes from there, he gains if its lineage is called kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow who must marry her late husband's brother (יבום)
Fell to him, meaning she became his to marry through יבום

phrases.english: Abaye said to them:
Do not listen to him,
it is a yevama who fell to him from there.
phrases.notes: In other words, he would want that place to count as kosher, so that he can marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי: לָא תְּצִיתוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the reporter of step 20 is reliable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reliability of רב איקא בר אבין's report
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone with a personal stake in a ruling is suspected of bending it in his own favor.

steps.title: רב איקא answers that the teaching is not his own
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא answers that he only passed on the ruling. It belongs to רב חננאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is it mine? It is רב חננאל's!
steps.whatsHappening: רב איקא defends himself. He did not invent the ruling; he is quoting his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suspicion of a personal interest only matters if the person made the ruling himself. Since the ruling comes from רב חננאל, who has no stake, רב איקא's interest is irrelevant.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it then...? (a question expressing surprise)

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it mine, then?
It is Rav Chananel's!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַטּוּ דִּידִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's suspicion in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts responsibility for the ruling to an earlier, neutral source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling might be tainted by רב איקא's personal interest.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling comes from רב חננאל, so it carries no personal bias.

steps.title: רב חננאל confirms the teaching in רב's name
steps.stepSummary: They go and ask רב חננאל, and he confirms that רב taught that חלזון ניהוונד counts like the גולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went and asked רב חננאל. He said to them: This is what רב said: חלזון ניהוונד is like the גולה regarding lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The people check the source directly, and רב חננאל confirms the ruling word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves that רב איקא reported accurately, so the ruling of step 20 stands. The גמרא repeats the exact wording to show it was confirmed exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that חלזון ניהוונד has kosher lineage is confirmed as truly from רב.

phrases.english: They went and asked Rav Chananel;
he said to them: This is what Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: חִלָּזוֹן נִיהֲוַונְד הֲרֵי הִיא כַּגּוֹלָה לְיוּחֲסִין.
phrases.english: Chillazon Nihavnad is like the Exile regarding lineage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזוּל שַׁיְילוּהּ לְרַב חֲנַנְאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the claim made in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the ruling of step 20 really comes from רב

steps.title: רבי אבא בר כהנא's opposing reading of the exile פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב's ruling disagrees with רבי אבא בר כהנא, who explains a פסוק about the exile of the ten tribes as naming חלזון, הדייב, גינזק, and either חמדן or ניהוונד with their neighboring towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי אבא בר כהנא. For רבי אבא בר כהנא said: What is meant by what is written: 'And he placed them in חלח and in חבור, the river גוזן, and the cities of מדי'? חלח is חלזון, חבור is הדייב, the river גוזן is גינזק, the cities of מדי are חמדן and its neighboring towns, and some say: ניהוונד and its neighboring towns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that another אמורא sees things differently. רבי אבא בר כהנא identifies the places where the ten tribes were exiled, and חלזון is on his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ten tribes were settled in חלזון and (by one version) in ניהוונד, their descendants mixed with the non-Jews there, so lineage from those places is doubtful. That clashes with רב's ruling that חלזון ניהוונד is as good as the גולה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written
And some say it this way

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging רב here. It is only noting that two אמוראים disagree about the status of these places.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana.
For Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:
What is meant by what is written:
"And he placed them in Chalach and in Chavor,
the river Gozan, and the cities of Madai"?
Chalach is Chillazon;
Chavor is Hadyav;
the river Gozan is Ginzak;
the cities of Madai are Chamadan and its neighboring towns;
and some say: this is Nihavnad and its neighboring towns.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows an opposing view to the ruling confirmed in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The places named in the exile פסוק, including חלזון and possibly ניהוונד, were settled by the ten tribes, which implies doubtful lineage there.

steps.title: Which towns are the neighboring towns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which towns are meant by 'its neighboring towns.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What are its neighboring towns?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for details. Which towns does 'its neighboring towns' include?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since these towns share the doubtful lineage status, it matters in practice to know exactly which ones they are.

phrases.english: What are its neighboring towns?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חַבְרוֹתֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term from step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the neighboring towns mentioned in step 24

steps.title: שמואל names the neighboring towns
steps.stepSummary: שמואל lists the neighboring towns: the city of מושכי, חוסקי, and רומקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The city of מושכי, חוסקי, and רומקי.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by naming the towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general phrase 'neighboring towns' now has a concrete list of three places.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: The city of Mushkhei,
Chuskei, and Rumkei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּרַךְ מוּשְׁכֵּי חוּסְקֵי וְרוּמְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The neighboring towns are מושכי, חוסקי, and רומקי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says all of them have flawed lineage
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that all these places have flawed lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And all of them are for flawed lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the practical ruling for the whole list: every one of these towns has doubtful lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the list into a real halachic ruling. Families from any of these towns may not be assumed to have kosher lineage.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: And all of them are for flawed lineage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְכוּלָּם לִפְסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the lineage status of the places listed in steps 24 and 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the listed places have flawed lineage.

steps.title: Challenge: שמואל elsewhere calls מושכני kosher
steps.stepSummary: Assuming מושכי is the same as מושכני, the גמרא challenges: שמואל himself said elsewhere that מושכני is like the גולה for lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was assumed that מושכי is the same as מושכני. But didn't רבי חייא בר אבין say that שמואל said: מושכני is like the גולה regarding lineage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a contradiction. מושכי is on the 'flawed' list, but שמואל called a town with an almost identical name kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem rests on assuming the two names refer to one town. If they do, שמואל contradicts himself: the same place cannot be both flawed and as good as the גולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A town with a name similar to מושכי

phrases.english: It was assumed:
Mushkhei is the same as Mushkenei.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiya bar Avin say that Shmuel said:
Mushkenei is like the Exile regarding lineage!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּא: מוּשְׁכֵּי הַיְינוּ מוּשְׁכְּנֵי. וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list of step 26 with another statement of שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's list of flawed towns that includes מושכי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מושכי and מושכני are one town, שמואל calls the same place both flawed and kosher.

steps.title: מושכי and מושכני are two different towns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מושכי and מושכני are separate places.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מושכי is separate and מושכני is separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by dropping the assumption that the two names are the same town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once they are two different towns, there is no contradiction. מושכי has flawed lineage, and מושכני is as good as the גולה.
steps.whatToRemember: Similar town names can hide different places: מושכי is flawed, while מושכני is like the גולה.

phrases.english: Rather, Mushkhei is separate and Mushkenei is separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מוּשְׁכֵּי לְחוּד וּמוּשְׁכְּנֵי לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes two places that seemed to be the same
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מושכי and מושכני are one town, so שמואל contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two different towns with different lineage status.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן on the three ribs in Daniel's vision
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the 'three ribs in its mouth' in דניאל's vision as חלזון, הדייב, and נציבין, which the kingdom sometimes swallows and sometimes spits out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth.' רבי יוחנן said: These are חלזון, הדייב, and נציבין, which it sometimes swallows and sometimes spits out.
steps.whatsHappening: Since these places came up, the גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's reading of a פסוק in דניאל about three of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bear in the vision stands for a kingdom, and the three ribs are three border towns. 'Swallows and spits out' means the towns keep passing in and out of that kingdom's control.

phrases.english: "And three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth."
Rabbi Yochanan said:
These are Chillazon, Hadyav, and Netzivin,
which it sometimes swallows
phrases.notes: He means the kingdom sometimes conquers these towns and sometimes loses them.

phrases.english: and sometimes spits out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְלָת עִלְעִין בְּפֻמַּהּ בֵּין שִׁנַּהּ. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related teaching about places named in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three ribs are חלזון, הדייב, and נציבין, border towns that keep changing hands.

steps.title: The second beast in דניאל's vision is Persia
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that the bear-like beast in דניאל's vision stands for the Persians, and gives four ways they resemble a bear.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And behold another beast, a second one, like a bear.' רב יוסף taught: These are the Persians. They eat and drink like a bear, they are heavy-bodied like a bear, they grow hair like a bear, and they have no rest like a bear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the vision in דניאל and quotes רב יוסף, who explains who the second beast is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, רבי יוחנן explained the 'three ribs in its mouth.' Now the גמרא goes back to the beginning of that same verse and identifies the bear itself as Persia. רב יוסף lists four bear-like traits to back up the identification.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (introduces a teaching of a תנא)

phrases.english: "And behold another beast, a second one, similar to a bear."
Rav Yosef taught: These are the Persians,
who eat and drink like a bear,
and are heavy-bodied like a bear,
and grow hair like a bear,
and have no rest like a bear.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: אֵלּוּ פָּרְסִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening words of the same פסוק whose ending רבי יוחנן explained in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bear in דניאל's vision represents Persia, which resembles a bear in four ways.

steps.title: רבי אמי calls a Persian rider a moving bear
steps.stepSummary: Whenever רבי אמי saw a Persian riding, he called him a bear on the move.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אמי saw a Persian riding, he would say: This is a moving bear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short story that supports רב יוסף's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי applies רב יוסף's idea to real life. The trait of 'no rest' is pictured as a Persian always riding from place to place.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami, when he would see
a Persian riding, would say:
This is a bear on the move.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי פָּרְסָא דְּרָכֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the Persian-bear comparison of step 31 being used in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A riding Persian is a living picture of the restless bear.

steps.title: רבי asks לוי to describe different groups
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks לוי to describe the Persians, the Persian priests (חברין), the Ishmaelites, and the Torah scholars of בבל. לוי answers each with a vivid comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to לוי: Describe the Persians to me. לוי said: They look like the armies of the house of דוד. Describe the חברין to me. They look like angels of destruction. Describe the Ishmaelites to me. They look like the demons of an outhouse. Describe the Torah scholars of בבל to me. They look like ministering angels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a conversation where רבי asks לוי to picture four groups for him, and לוי gives a comparison for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Persians are compared to the soldiers of דוד's armies. The חברין are compared to destroying angels, and the Ishmaelites to outhouse demons. The Torah scholars of בבל get the highest praise: they are compared to ministering angels.

phrases.english: Rabbi said to Levi:
Show me Persians.
phrases.notes: רבי means: describe for me what they look like.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דּוֹמִים לַחֲיָילוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית דָּוִד.
phrases.english: He said to him: They are like the armies of the house of David.
Show me Ḥabbarin.
They are like angels of destruction.
Show me Ishmaelites.
They are like the demons of an outhouse.
Show me the Torah scholars in Babylonia.
They are like ministering angels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְלֵוִי: הַרְאֵנִי פָּרְסִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the Persians from step 31, now through a conversation between רבי and לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי describes the Persians, חברין, Ishmaelites, and Babylonian Torah scholars with four vivid comparisons.

steps.title: On his deathbed, רבי names places in בבל with lineage problems
steps.stepSummary: As he was dying, רבי said that all of הומניא are עמונים, all of מסגריא are ממזרים, and that in בירקא two brothers swap wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי was dying, he said: There is a place called הומניא in בבל, and all of it is עמונים. There is a place called מסגריא in בבל, and all of it is ממזרים. There is a place called בירקא in בבל, and there are two brothers there who swap their wives with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי's last words, in which he warns about specific towns in בבל whose people have problems with יוחסין (family lineage).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the daf's main theme of which places have pure or flawed lineage. Unlike the earlier general statements, רבי names exact towns and exact problems: an Ammonite population, a population of ממזרים, and a wife-swapping arrangement that would make the children ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: When he was dying (literally 'when his soul was at rest')

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the aggadic stories back to the practical question of the daf: which families one may marry into.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה נִיחָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲמַר:
phrases.english: When Rabbi was dying, he said:
There is Homanya in Babylonia –
all of it is Ammonites.
There is Masgariya in Babylonia –
all of it is mamzerim.
There is Bireka in Babylonia –
there are two brothers [in it]
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: who swap their wives with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה נִיחָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic descriptions of nations and returns to the daf's theme of flawed lineage in specific places, as in steps 26-27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הומניא is entirely עמונים, מסגריא is entirely ממזרים, and in בירקא two brothers swap wives.

steps.title: The town of בירתא דסטיא abandons Judaism
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that בירתא דסטיא turned away from God that day. They caught fish on שבת, were put in excommunication, and then left Judaism entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a place called בירתא דסטיא in בבל. Today they turned away from God. A pond of fish overflowed on שבת, and they went and caught the fish on שבת. רבי אחי son of רבי יאשיה put them in excommunication, and they became apostates.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's list continues with a town whose problem is not lineage but leaving Judaism, and the גמרא explains what happened there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'today' shows רבי was speaking about something happening at that very time. The people broke שבת by catching fish. When they were punished with excommunication (שמתא), they abandoned the Jewish people altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: They became apostates, left the faith

phrases.english: There is Bireta DeSatya in Babylonia –
today they turned away from God,
for a pond full of fish overflowed on Shabbat,
and they went and trapped them on Shabbat,
and Rabbi Aḥai son of Rabbi Yoshiya excommunicated them,
and they became apostates.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּירְתָּא דְּסָטְיָא אִיכָּא בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in רבי's deathbed list, this time about leaving Judaism rather than lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בירתא דסטיא broke שבת, was excommunicated, and abandoned Judaism.

steps.title: רבי mentions אדא בר אהבה in אקרא דאגמא
steps.stepSummary: רבי's list continues: in the town of אקרא דאגמא there is a man named אדא בר אהבה. What he says about him comes in the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a place called אקרא דאגמא in בבל, and אדא בר אהבה is there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next item in רבי's list. It names a person in a certain town, and the point about him comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This item changes the pattern. Instead of describing a town's problem, רבי names one specific person who lives there. The reason for mentioning him is explained in the continuation of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in בבל (name means 'fortress of the marsh')
An אמורא, named here by רבי

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as another lineage problem. רבי's statement about אדא בר אהבה is not finished yet and continues in the next part of the daf.

phrases.english: There is Akra DeAgma in Babylonia –
Adda bar Ahava is in it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקְרָא דְאַגְמָא אִיכָּא בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי's deathbed list, now naming a specific person instead of a town's problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי points to אדא בר אהבה in אקרא דאגמא; the point is completed in the continuation.
